public_rationale: This forecast has no deadline. It concerns the order in which AI masters physical and psychological reasoning, and whether AGI arrives gradually. Evaluations found in the search show models still below human level in both areas, so the order cannot be judged yet. AGI has not clearly arrived, so the 'no magic day' part cannot be judged either. No decisive event settles either part early.
limitations: The ordering claim has no defined thresholds.
The evidence on how theory-of-mind and physics benchmarks compare is mixed and changes quickly.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI physical reasoning will improve before psychological reasoning, and AGI will not arrive on a single identifiable day.

statement.excerpt: I expect for example that physical reasoning will improve (a radical boon for domestic robots) before psychological reasoning; there won’t be a magic day in which we say “aha AGI landed on January 27, 2062” or whatever it is.
statement.document_title: AGI will not happen in your lifetime. Or will it?

from_speaker: there won't be a magic day
our_interpretation: Two parts. (1) AI will reach strong everyday physical reasoning before strong psychological (theory-of-mind) reasoning. (2) AGI will arrive gradually rather than on a single identifiable day.
No deadline is stated. Both parts concern the path to AGI, which had not been reached by the evaluation date.
criteria.support_condition: Once AI reaches reliable, general physical and psychological reasoning, dated evidence shows physical reasoning got there first, and AGI's arrival has no single agreed date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Dated evidence that AI reached reliable psychological reasoning clearly before reliable physical reasoning, or that AGI arrived as a single, widely recognised discrete event.
